skill-partial-scaffoldskill-scaffolding0 of 0.375 (major)failThe requirement is that when some anchors are present, the skill scaffolds every missing anchor and leaves the existing ones alone. SKILL.md (lines 79-80 and 87-90) says the bootstrap helper does this: only the missing anchors are added and missing dependencies are merged. But the helper does not fully add a missing build anchor. In detectAnchors (scaffold.mjs 89-92), the build anchor counts as present only if pkg.scripts.build is a string. The repo&#39;s own test (scaffold.test.ts 73-74) confirms that a package.json without a build script means the build anchor is missing. Now take a partial scaffold where the kit and index are present but the existing package.json has no build script. resolveTarget reuses the root (127-128) and returns missing = [&#39;build&#39;] (137). In bootstrap, the template package.json belongs to the build anchor but is skipped because the file exists (194-197). The helper then calls mergePackageJson with scripts: anchors.includes(&#39;kit&#39;) (202). Since anchors is [&#39;build&#39;], scripts is false, so only dependencies and devDependencies are merged (161) and the build script is never added. The build anchor is still missing after bootstrap, so the &#39;scaffolds the missing anchors&#39; clause is not met. The review guidance says to fail when a delivered helper script implements the branch differently from what is required. This is the partial-scaffold branch the criterion names, not an unnamed hypothetical. Judges A and C are right that the helper filters template files by anchorOf, skips existing files, and merges dependencies, so it preserves existing anchors. But that only covers the &#39;without disturbing&#39; clause. It does not show that every missing anchor gets scaffolded, and the source above shows a missing build anchor that does not. That reason does not decide the criterion. The requirement fails a test only when it sleeps for a fixed time instead of waiting for state before asserting the step. Here the settle runs only after the polled waitForFunction on the step index has succeeded, and the index is checked again before capture. There are three browser-driving test files: e2e-001-verify, e2e-002-failures and int-002-inspect. int-001-bootstrap also runs `npm run verify` on bootstrapped apps. All four are quoted in full. None of them drives Playwright directly or calls a fixed sleep. Each one awaits a subprocess through run() and asserts only after the child has closed. In tests/helpers/proc.ts, run() uses setTimeout only as a process-group kill timeout, and clears it on &#39;close&#39;. It never stands in for a wait on state. In e2e-002, setTimeout appears at line 97 only inside an injected-fault source string that runs in the page under test. Inside the scripts these tests run, every step advance is a polling wait on observable state. verify.mjs:96 and inspect-presentation.mjs:77 press ArrowRight and then call page.waitForFunction until data-step-index equals the target, with a 4000 ms timeout. A failure throws. After that, verify reads data-step-index again and fails on a mismatch (lines 104-105). inspect checks snapshot.index !== i before it captures (line 84). Judges A and B gave pass, and the material bears out their reasoning. Judge C says int-002 relies on a fixed settle delay, because inspect calls deps.settle(settleMs), which awaits setTimeout (inspect-presentation.mjs:82; diagnostics.mjs:54-56). That reason does not decide the criterion. The requirement fails a test only when it sleeps for a fixed time instead of waiting for state before asserting the step. Here the settle runs only after the polled waitForFunction on the step index has succeeded, and the index is checked again before capture. The int-002 assertions on runningAnimationsAtCapture read a report written after the subprocess exits; that report is not taken after a sleep that replaces a state wait. The guidance also says fixed settle delays are validator noise, so they neither earn nor lose credit. SKILL.md (lines 79-80 and 87-90) says the bootstrap helper does this: only the missing anchors are added and missing dependencies are merged. But the helper does not fully add a missing build anchor. In detectAnchors (scaffold.mjs 89-92), the build anchor counts as present only if pkg.scripts.build is a string. The repo&#39;s own test (scaffold.test.ts 73-74) confirms that a package.json without a build script means the build anchor is missing. Now take a partial scaffold where the kit and index are present but the existing package.json has no build script. resolveTarget reuses the root (127-128) and returns missing = [&#39;build&#39;] (137). In bootstrap, the template package.json belongs to the build anchor but is skipped because the file exists (194-197). The helper then calls mergePackageJson with scripts: anchors.includes(&#39;kit&#39;) (202). Since anchors is [&#39;build&#39;], scripts is false, so only dependencies and devDependencies are merged (161) and the build script is never added. The build anchor is still missing after bootstrap, so the &#39;scaffolds the missing anchors&#39; clause is not met. The review guidance says to fail when a delivered helper script implements the branch differently from what is required. This is the partial-scaffold branch the criterion names, not an unnamed hypothetical. Judges A and C are right that the helper filters template files by anchorOf, skips existing files, and merges dependencies, so it preserves existing anchors. But that only covers the &#39;without disturbing&#39; clause. It does not show that every missing anchor gets scaffolded, and the source above shows a missing build anchor that does not. Judge B&#39;s reason holds up against the source and decides the criterion.","evidence":["scaffold.mjs 89-92: the build anchor requires typeof pkg.scripts?.build === The browser tests (int-002, e2e-001, e2e-002) start the inspect or verify script as a subprocess through `run()` in tests/helpers/proc.ts. That helper awaits the child&#39;s `close` event. Its only `setTimeout` is a kill-on-timeout safety timer that is cleared when the child closes, so it is not used as a wait. Inside the scripts, every step change is awaited by polling: `page.waitForFunction` checks that `data-step-index` equals the target step, with a 4000 ms timeout (inspect-presentation.mjs:77, verify.mjs:96). Inspect then reads `snapshot.index` back and confirms it before capturing (inspect-presentation.mjs:84). The tests make their assertions only after the process exits, using its output, report.json and the PNG files. A search of tests/ found no `waitForTimeout` or sleep call. The only other `setTimeout` is inside a string injected as a fault in e2e-002:97. The `sleep` in inspect-diagnostics.test.ts belongs to an injected fake clock that does not really wait. Judge A and Judge B: their cited material bears this out, and it decides the requirement. Judge C: it is true that int-002:54-74 asserts `runningAnimationsAtCapture` is 0 after the script&#39;s default 900 ms settle, and that `settle()` in scripts/lib/diagnostics.mjs:54-56 waits a fixed time. uses a fixed sleep, and step waits poll observable state. There are three browser-driving test files: e2e-001-verify, e2e-002-failures and int-002-inspect. int-001-bootstrap also runs `npm run verify` on bootstrapped apps. All four are quoted in full. None of them drives Playwright directly or calls a fixed sleep. Each one awaits a subprocess through run() and asserts only after the child has closed. In tests/helpers/proc.ts, run() uses setTimeout only as a process-group kill timeout, and clears it on &#39;close&#39;. It never stands in for a wait on state. In e2e-002, setTimeout appears at line 97 only inside an injected-fault source string that runs in the page under test. Inside the scripts these tests run, every step advance is a polling wait on observable state. verify.mjs:96 and inspect-presentation.mjs:77 press ArrowRight and then call page.waitForFunction until data-step-index equals the target, with a 4000 ms timeout. A failure throws. After that, verify reads data-step-index again and fails on a mismatch (lines 104-105). inspect checks snapshot.index !== i before it captures (line 84). Judges A and B gave pass, and the material bears out their reasoning. Judge C says int-002 relies on a fixed settle delay, because inspect calls deps.settle(settleMs), which awaits setTimeout (inspect-presentation.mjs:82; diagnostics.mjs:54-56). That reason does not decide the criterion. The requirement fails a test only when it sleeps for a fixed time instead of waiting for state before asserting the step. Here the settle runs only after the polled waitForFunction on the step index has succeeded, and the index is checked again before capture. The int-002 assertions on runningAnimationsAtCapture read a report written after the subprocess exits; that report is not taken after a sleep that replaces a state wait. The guidance also says fixed settle delays are validator noise, so they neither earn nor lose credit. I therefore rule the verdict of judges A and B: pass.","evidence":["tests/helpers/proc.ts:14-29 run(): spawns the child and resolves on &#39;close&#39;. Judges A and B gave pass, and the material bears out their reasoning. Judge C says int-002 relies on a fixed settle delay, because inspect calls deps.settle(settleMs), which awaits setTimeout (inspect-presentation.mjs:82; diagnostics.mjs:54-56). That reason does not decide the criterion. The requirement fails a test only when it sleeps for a fixed time instead of waiting for state before asserting the step. Here the settle runs only after the polled waitForFunction on the step index has succeeded, and the index is checked again before capture. The int-002 assertions on runningAnimationsAtCapture read a report written after the subprocess exits; that report is not taken after a sleep that replaces a state wait. Consider a project where the kit and the index are present, but the existing package.json has no `build` script. `detectAnchors` reports `build` as false, because it requires `typeof pkg.scripts?.build === &#39;string&#39;`. `resolveTarget` then reuses the root, since `rootAnchors.kit` is true, and returns `missing = [&#39;build&#39;]`. In `bootstrap`, the template&#39;s package.json counts as a build-anchor file, but it is skipped because the file already exists. The function then calls `mergePackageJson(..., { scripts: anchors.includes(&#39;kit&#39;) })`. Here `anchors` is `[&#39;build&#39;]`, so `scripts` is false and only `dependencies` and `devDependencies` are merged. The `build` script is never added, so the build anchor stays missing after bootstrap, and SKILL.md says to run bootstrap and then proceed. The fixture requires that missing anchors are scaffolded. The review guidance says to fail an instruction-governed scaffold criterion when a delivered helper script implements that branch differently.
